note: South Korea: a foreigner engaging in paid artistic or entertainment work (music, theatre, performance, advertising and the like) needs the Arts and Entertainment status of stay (E-6), the E-6-1 arts and entertainment kind on a recommendation from the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism (Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Act, art. 12 and Table 1-2). No days of such work without it are named. Read first from a 2026 law-firm guide quoting the Decree (2026-10-29; it answered 403 on 2026-11-03). The Decree itself was read 2026-11-03 on the National Law Information Center (as in force from 2 October 2026, Presidential Decree 36728): art. 12 and Annex 1-2, row 19, 예술흥행 (E-6), for paid music, art and literature and for entertainment, performance, theatre, sport, advertising and fashion modelling. The E-6-1 kind and the Ministry of Culture's recommendation aren't in the Decree (they are the Ministry of Justice's guidelines, not read), so the entry stays secondary on them.

sources.title: KLawGuru, Korea's E-6 (Arts and Entertainment) Visa: A Practical Guide (7 August 2026)
sources.said: The E-6 visa is a residence status for Arts and Entertainment activities (예술흥행). Under Article 12 of the Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Control Act and its attached Table 1-2, it is granted to foreigners who intend to engage in profit-generating artistic activities such as music, fine art, or literature, or profit-oriented activities such as entertainment, musical performance, theater, athletics, advertising/fashion modeling, or equivalent activities
